abaqusFeature: Acoustic impedance interaction (surface impedance boundary contribution)
summary: For an AC3D20 face, integrate the real-positive locally reacting impedance damping contribution C_ij = integral_S(N_i N_j/Z)dS and report the face area and matrix alongside the existing acoustic element results.
selector: Optional boundaryImpedance object {face: S1..S6, impedance: positive finite real}; omission preserves the existing output shape and numerical results.
limitations: Element-level host-f64 operation for AC3D20 faces only. It implements a real positive local-reacting impedance term in transient pressure damping form; complex/frequency-dependent impedance, incident waves, infinite elements, global assembly, boundary condition application, and Abaqus execution/parity are not provided. Existing module identity and CalculiX provenance remain unchanged.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Standard direct-solution steady-state dynamics for coupled acoustic-structural response
summary: Adds a bounded two-coordinate complex harmonic response for the existing reduced structural-acoustic mass, stiffness, and coupling model with diagonal viscous damping; returns both complex responses and the equation residual.
selector: method=method-harmonic-response; structuralMass, structuralStiffness, acousticMass, acousticStiffness, frequency, optional coupling, structuralDamping, acousticDamping, structuralForce, acousticForce
limitations: Host-f64 reduced two-DOF model only; loads are in-phase real amplitudes and damping is diagonal viscous. It does not assemble FE matrices, calculate acoustic mesh/interface coupling, modal superposition, frequency sweeps, material damping, or establish Abaqus parity. Explicit GPU requests are unsupported.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Standard steady-state dynamics acoustic outputs GRADP (acoustic pressure gradient) and ACV (acoustic particle velocity)
summary: Adds opt-in analytic pressure-gradient and particle-velocity vectors at probe points from the existing truncated rigid-cavity modal solution, while preserving default output and pressure results.
selector: includeAcousticKinematics: true; host-f64 only (auto selects host, explicit CUDA is rejected)
limitations: Clean-room analytic modal result for a rigid rectangular cavity with a point monopole and truncated modes; pressure gradient and particle velocity are host-f64 only. It is not general finite-element assembly, coupled acoustics, open-boundary radiation, or full Abaqus parity.

abaqusFeature: C3D10 second-order tetrahedron consistent mass matrix in stress/displacement analysis
summary: Adds method consistent-mass, assembling the 30x30 translational consistent element mass matrix from rho times the integral of N_i N_j dV for an affine straight-sided C3D10. A fixed 64-point Duffy-transformed Gauss-Legendre rule exactly integrates the degree-four reference integrand; curved C3D10 geometry is explicitly unsupported for this method.
selector: method=consistent-mass with density>0 and ten ordered C3D10 nodes; accepts optional backend=host|cpu|auto
limitations: One affine straight-sided C3D10 with constant positive density; output is the element consistent translational mass matrix only, with no rotational DOFs, global assembly, constraints, time integration, or dynamic response. Abaqus documents a 15-point scheme for general second-order tetrahedra; this implementation's 64-point transformed rule is an exact host-side construction for the restricted affine case and does not claim Abaqus numerical or solver parity.

abaqusFeature: *OPERATOR OUTPUT, MASS (Abaqus/Standard); material *DENSITY
summary: Computes a uniform-density consistent translational 60x60 element mass matrix for C3D20 or C3D20R using 3x3x3 mass quadrature for either element variant; reports integrated volume and total mass.
selector: Set method=mass-matrix and provide density (or alias rho), element, and 20 nodes in existing C3D20 ordering.
limitations: Element-level host-f64 calculation only. Assumes one finite positive uniform density and the reference geometry; no spatial or temperature dependence, rotary inertia, mass scaling, global assembly, constraints, loads, or transient/eigenvalue solution. The mass integral uses 3x3x3 quadrature for both variants; C3D20R's reduced 2x2x2 rule applies to the existing stiffness operation only. This shared CalculiX-named mathematical routine is not a claim of full Abaqus or CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: C3D8 full-integration element field outputs E, S, and Mises stress at integration points
summary: Optional nodalDisplacements input recovers infinitesimal total strain, thermal-eigenstrain-corrected isotropic linear-elastic stress, Mises stress, and elastic energy density at all eight 2x2x2 Gauss points.
selector: nodalDisplacements: optional array of exactly 8 finite [ux, uy, uz] triples in the established C3D8 node order; supplying it adds result.integrationPointFields.
limitations: One isolated small-strain C3D8 with constant isotropic linear elasticity and full 2x2x2 integration. Thermal correction is a uniform alpha*dT eigenstrain. No finite-strain kinematics, nonlinear/plastic constitutive updates, global assembly, boundary conditions, contact, coupled temperature DOFs, or claim of complete Abaqus/CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Explicit diagonal lumped element mass matrix for C3D8R; *DENSITY material data
summary: Adds opt-in row-summed nodal translational masses from density and 2x2x2 isoparametric quadrature, with optional nodal-velocity kinetic energy.
selector: massMode="lumped" with positive density; optional velocity has 24 finite nodal components.
limitations: Single linear isotropic element only. Computes clean-room row-summed translational nodal mass and optional kinetic energy; no assembled model, mass scaling, spatial density distribution, rotational inertia, explicit time integration, or Abaqus/CalculiX parity is claimed.

abaqusFeature: *DAMAGE INITIATION, ACCUMULATION POWER
summary: Integrates the ductile or Johnson-Cook material-point damage initiation index using a configurable positive power on each normalized plastic-strain increment; the default power 1 preserves existing linear accumulation, and crossing strain is interpolated consistently with the selected power.
selector: accumulationPower (optional positive finite exponent; defaults to 1)
limitations: Host-only single material-point history for ductile and Johnson-Cook failure-strain criteria. The selected Johnson-Cook accumulation-power mapping is documented for Abaqus/Explicit. It does not assemble elements, solve equilibrium, feed damage back into stress, or delete elements; it does not implement general Abaqus material, rate-dependent ductile tables, or full Abaqus/CalculiX equivalence. The power law is applied to caller-supplied increments using each increment's current failure strain.

abaqusFeature: *INITIAL CONDITIONS, TYPE=ROTATING VELOCITY
summary: Builds nodal velocity vectors from angular speed, axis endpoints, translational velocity, and per-node coordinates using v = vg + omega e x (X-Xa); existing explicit temperature, displacement, velocity, stress, and plastic-strain field assembly remains available.
selector: condition type rotating-velocity with omega, axisA, axisB, optional translation, coordinates, and count
limitations: Host-f64 field assembly only; coordinates are supplied directly in one consistent unit system, and no mesh, node-set, integration-point, equilibrium, or Abaqus solver semantics are evaluated. Does not claim full Abaqus or CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: *EXPANSION with a uniform *TEMPERATURE field
summary: Computes the consistent element thermal equivalent nodal load from linear isotropic expansion strain for CAX3/CAX4 axisymmetric continua.
selector: method=thermal-load; provide E, nu, expansionCoefficient (or alpha), and deltaTemperature
limitations: Host-f64 single-element linear elasticity only, for uniform temperature increment and constant isotropic expansion coefficient. It returns an equivalent load; it does not solve temperatures, assemble a model, apply constraints, or reproduce all Abaqus/CalculiX behaviors. No vendor-code equivalence is claimed.

abaqusFeature: *CLEARANCE initial clearance/overclosure; Abaqus/Standard signed values, Abaqus/Explicit non-negative values
summary: Adds an opt-in Abaqus analysis-product selector to the existing local small-sliding clearance calculation. Standard accepts signed initial clearance values to represent overclosure; Explicit continues to reject negative values. Derived gap, pressure, and heat-flux overflow is rejected.
selector: analysisProduct: standard|explicit (default explicit preserves the prior non-negative clearance input contract)
limitations: One local scalar contact point only, using a linearized signed gap and the pre-existing penalty response. It does not implement Abaqus contact tracking, finite-element assembly, surface projection, solver iterations, or full Abaqus/CalculiX parity. Abaqus/Explicit input is restricted to non-negative initial clearance values.

abaqusFeature: *CONTROLS, PARAMETERS=LINE SEARCH (Abaqus/Standard)
summary: Adds an opt-in residual-vector line-search policy that applies bounded trial scales and the documented maximum search count, scale bounds, residual reduction threshold, and eta contraction; reports honest acceptance and iteration status.
selector: method=abaqus-controls; r0 and w required; optional maxLineSearch, scaleMax, scaleMin, residualReduction, eta
limitations: Scalar host-f64 residual-line exercise only. It does not assemble finite elements, compute Abaqus residuals, reproduce Abaqus internal interpolation, or claim full Abaqus/CalculiX parity; explicit CUDA requests fail closed.

abaqusFeature: *CONTROLS, PARAMETERS=FIELD, CONVERGENCE CHECK=STRICT|RELAXED
summary: Adds optional residual-plus-correction strict convergence and correction-only relaxed convergence for a single linear CSR field, using max|dx|/max|x| as the correction ratio; the existing residual-only behavior remains the default.
selector: convergenceCheck=residual|strict|relaxed and optional positive correctionTol
limitations: This is a bounded single-field linear-system analogue, not Abaqus nonlinear increment convergence: it has no time-averaged or maximum field-flux scaling, contact/discontinuity logic, multiphysics field selection, or Abaqus execution. The Abaqus strict and relaxed feature mapping does not imply parity with the commercial solver. The moderate criterion is explicitly unsupported because the CSR contract supplies no field-flux scale.

abaqusFeature: *FRICTION (classical isotropic Coulomb friction)
summary: Adds an opt-in single-contact-point Coulomb return map. Existing normal penalty pressure defines the limit mu*p; a signed trial tangential traction is retained in stick or clipped to that limit in slip. Reports the friction limit and stick/slip state.
selector: method=coulomb; requires finite frictionMu >= 0 and finite tangentialTrial
limitations: Host-f64 scalar local contact calculation only: one normal gap and one signed tangential traction. Uses the existing penalty normal law; no surface discretization, vector two-direction norm, history evolution, temperature/slip-rate-dependent coefficient, anisotropy, equilibrium iteration, or full Abaqus/CalculiX equivalence.

abaqusFeature: *EXPANSION isotropic thermal expansion in a plane-strain solid
summary: Computes a uniform constant-alpha thermal eigenstrain increment for a single linear elastic CPE element, including plane-strain thermal stress offsets, equivalent nodal thermal forces, and recoverable element energy alongside its existing stiffness response.
selector: method-calculix-cpe-stiffness with paired thermalExpansion and temperatureChange inputs
limitations: Single isolated linear elastic 2-D plane-strain element with uniform temperature increment and constant isotropic expansion coefficient. Does not solve temperature fields, assemble meshes, apply boundary conditions, or support temperature-dependent/anisotropic expansion, nonlinear material response, or full Abaqus parity. Host f64 only.

abaqusFeature: *EXPANSION, TYPE=ISO
summary: For CPS4/CPS4R, computes uniform isotropic secant thermal free strain alpha*deltaT and its consistent element equivalent nodal load using the selected element quadrature.
selector: Optional paired scalar inputs expansionCoefficient and temperatureChange on the existing stiffness request.
limitations: Single linear-elastic plane-stress QUAD4 element; constant isotropic secant expansion coefficient and uniform temperature change only. Reports free strain and equivalent nodal RHS load; does not solve global equilibrium or thermal conduction, support temperature/field-dependent or anisotropic expansion, or claim full Abaqus/CalculiX equivalence. Existing displacement recovery remains the mechanical-only response.

abaqusFeature: *SELECT CYCLIC SYMMETRY MODES (NMIN, NMAX, EVEN)
summary: Adds Abaqus-style inclusive nodal-diameter range selection and EVEN-only filtering for cyclic symmetry modal reductions, preserving explicit harmonic selection and defaults.
selector: modeSelection: {nmin?, nmax?, evenOnly?}; mutually exclusive with harmonics.
limitations: Host-f64 reduced real-vector sector matrices only; no Abaqus solver call, surface-based tie constraints, unmatched-mesh interpolation, load mapping, or full Standard eigenfrequency procedure. Preserves CalculiX module identity and is not a claim of suite parity.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/CAE Angular transformation of nodal vector results in a cylindrical coordinate system with deformation effects
summary: Adds an opt-in deformed vector frame: each cylindrical nodal basis is evaluated at reference position plus the supplied displacement, then local/global nodal vectors are projected through that frame. Reference nodal coordinates and frames remain separately reported.
selector: Set vectorFrame to deformed and provide one finite displacement 3-vector per node; default vectorFrame is reference.
limitations: Host-f64 coordinate postprocessing only; it does not solve structural response or reproduce all Abaqus output transformation modes. Uses supplied nodal displacement vectors and their deformed locations; no interpolation, finite element fields, deformation scaling, spherical systems, or proprietary Abaqus/CalculiX solver behavior is implemented. Existing sw-calculix module ID, defaults, and provenance are retained.

abaqusFeature: Distributing coupling constraint influence radius (*COUPLING, INFLUENCE RADIUS)
summary: Optional spherical influence-radius filtering of caller-supplied coupling-region nodes before the existing weighted distributing load or motion calculation; nodes on the radius boundary are included.
selector: influenceRadius (optional positive finite radius in coordinate units)
limitations: Host-f64 nodal selection over the supplied region only. Caller supplies candidate nodes and weights; this does not integrate cut element facets, generate surface tributary weights, assemble a global FE system, reproduce solver constraint enforcement, or claim full Abaqus/CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: *EXPANSION with DEFINITION=SECANT and Standard tangent thermal expansion
summary: Adds opt-in Abaqus material-point secant and tangent thermal expansion definitions with initial-state strain subtraction/integration while preserving legacy defaults.
selector: definition=secant|tangent; optional initialTemperature and existing zeroTemperature/expansion table
limitations: Material-point isotropic calculation only; no element assembly, field-variable dependence, orthotropy, coupled equilibrium, or full Abaqus parity. Tangent formulation corresponds to Abaqus/Standard capability.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Explicit *DYNAMIC, EXPLICIT central-difference integration
summary: Adds an opt-in damped central-difference time integrator for a linear scalar oscillator, reports interpolated integer-time velocity, and rejects time increments above the single-mode stability limit.
selector: method="explicit"; existing method defaults and implicit methods are preserved.
limitations: Host-f64 scalar linear SDOF only with constant or sampled force history and viscous damping. The stability bound uses the oscillator's single frequency; there is no mesh eigenvalue estimate, nonlinear material, contact, multi-DOF solve, automatic time incrementation, or full Abaqus/Explicit parity. Explicit CUDA requests remain unsupported.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Explicit *CLOAD in a *DYNAMIC, EXPLICIT procedure
summary: Adds constant applied nodal force to explicit SDOF and uniform 1D bar central-difference equations and includes its potential in the discrete energy diagnostic.
selector: analysis.appliedForce (scalar for SDOF; scalar broadcast or one value per node for bar)
limitations: Linear lumped SDOF or uniform 1D bar only; force is constant for the whole step and no Abaqus amplitude, contact, nonlinear material, general mesh, or full commercial solver behavior is implemented. Nonzero appliedForce requires the host-f64 path; the pre-existing zero-load CUDA path remains available.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Explicit ELPD and EPDDEN plastic dissipated energy outputs
summary: Integrates the exact material-point plastic dissipation density q d(ep_eq) during isotropic J2 return mapping and reports per-step and cumulative values, including piecewise-linear hardening and its plateau.
selector: Always included in the existing sw-calculix-plasticity response as history[].plasticDissipationIncrement, history[].plasticDissipation, and summary.finalPlasticDissipation; no new input selector.
limitations: Single small-strain 3D J2 material point with associative flow and isotropic hardening; energy density only. No mesh, element integration, whole-model ALLPD balance, rate/temperature dependence, or full Abaqus/CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Explicit central-difference integration with material *DAMPING, ALPHA mass-proportional Rayleigh damping
summary: Adds opt-in mass-proportional damping C=alpha M to the lumped SDOF/spring-chain central-difference recurrence, calculates the damping-adjusted critical increment, and reports a discrete viscous dissipation energy balance.
selector: model.alpha (finite, >= 0; default 0.0)
limitations: Clean-room reduced linear lumped-mass SDOF/spring-chain model only. Implements mass-proportional alpha damping; stiffness-proportional beta, general material/element damping, nonlinear constitutive behavior, FE assembly, contact, and automatic element time incrementation are not implemented. This is a bounded mathematical mapping, not full Abaqus or CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Standard transient uncoupled heat transfer with *FILM boundary conditions
summary: Adds an opt-in 1-D cell-centred finite-volume transient conduction mode with implicit theta integration and convective film exchange to an ambient at both ends. The half-cell conduction and film resistances are combined, then solved as a tridiagonal system.
selector: method=film-1d; boundary={type:film, ambient, coefficient, conductivity}; theta retains its existing [0,1] meaning/default.
limitations: Constant properties and a uniform 1-D line only; identical film data is applied at both ends. Uses a cell-centred finite-volume discretization and prescribed uniform time increments, with no finite-element assembly, nonlinear material behavior, radiation, volumetric source, or Abaqus input-deck execution. This is a bounded corresponding capability, not full Abaqus or CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Explicit general-contact preferred frictional-work distribution factors (SURFACE PROPERTY ASSIGNMENT, PROPERTY=DISTRIBUTION FACTOR)
summary: Opt-in normalized split of local Coulomb frictional dissipation between two contacting surfaces, including per-increment and accumulated work with conservation checks. Existing traction and dissipation behavior is unchanged when the selector is absent.
selector: workDistribution { preferredA, preferredB }
limitations: Host-f64 local penalty Coulomb contact-point return map only; this does not solve Abaqus contact, surfaces, thermal transport, or a finite-element model. The work partition follows documented Abaqus/Explicit preferred-factor normalization and is not a claim of full Abaqus or CalculiX equivalence.

abaqusFeature: *HYPERELASTIC with uniaxial test data, including predicted traction-free lateral contraction
summary: Adds a compressible uniaxial material-point mode that solves the equal lateral stretch from zero transverse Cauchy stress for the existing hyperelastic potentials.
selector: method=method-hyperelastic-uniaxial-free with stretch and existing model constants
limitations: Host-f64 single material point only; assumes equal lateral stretches and solves their common value so sigma22=sigma33=0. It does not calibrate coefficients from a test curve or model a specimen, mesh, element formulation, contact, or global equilibrium, and it does not claim Abaqus parity.

abaqusFeature: *ENERGY OUTPUT, ALLPD (related plastic energy output; material-point yield-work measure only)
summary: Opt-in accumulated equivalent-yield work density computed by trapezoidal integration of yield stress over equivalent plastic strain, emitted per increment and in the summary, and restartable through state.plasticWorkDensity.
selector: plasticWork=true
limitations: Small-strain host-f64 material-point J2 model only; no FE assembly, mesh integration, element volume weighting, or solver energy balance. plasticWorkDensity integrates isotropic equivalent yield stress against equivalent plastic strain with per-increment trapezoidal quadrature (exact for linear hardening and approximate across tabulated slope changes); it is a material-point yield-work measure related to Abaqus plastic energy output and is not an ALLPD-equivalent value or full Abaqus/CalculiX parity. CUDA requests remain unsupported.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Standard linear multiple load cases in a linear perturbation step (*LOAD CASE)
summary: Optionally solves up to 16 independent right-hand-side load vectors against one selected built-in SPD stiffness matrix, reusing one sparse LDL^T factorization and reporting each displacement vector and residual.
selector: loadCases: nonempty array of 1-16 finite right-hand-side arrays, each matching the selected problem size; requires one SPD problem and the sparse LDL^T path.
limitations: Teaching-scale host-f64 algebra over built-in example matrices only (n <= 256; at most 16 load cases). It does not parse Abaqus decks, assemble finite-element operators, interpret Abaqus load definitions or base states, support indefinite matrices for this option, or provide full Abaqus/CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Standard *STATIC, NLGEOM with tabular *AMPLITUDE-style step factors
summary: Solves a geometrically nonlinear total-Lagrangian SVK bar/truss equilibrium with bounded Newton increments and optionally applies a shared relative amplitude factor at each increment to nodal loads and prescribed displacements.
selector: Optional loadFactors array; when supplied it contains one finite factor per step and infers steps if steps is omitted. Omission preserves the existing linear ramp.
limitations: Host-f64 implementation for pin-jointed 2D/3D SVK bars only. loadFactors are shared by every applied load and prescribed displacement and sampled once per fixed increment; there is no time interpolation, adaptive incrementation, continuum/shell element, contact, follower load, or full Abaqus/CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: *CREEP, LAW=TIME (Norton time-hardening creep)
summary: Adds opt-in exact and independently Euler-checked integration of Norton/Bailey-Norton creep under a bounded contiguous piecewise-constant stress history, retaining absolute time across increments.
selector: stressHistory: array of {start,end,stress} intervals; existing A, n, m, time0, time, steps, and scalar stress inputs remain required.
limitations: Material-point scalar Norton/time-hardening integration only; assumes constant stress within each interval, does not solve equilibrium or multiaxial flow, temperature or field dependencies, creep-time reset, automatic increments, or target-strain inversion for histories. This clean-room operation is not full Abaqus or CalculiX parity; the stress-history extension is host-f64 only.

abaqusFeature: *ORIENTATION with *ELASTIC orthotropic material
summary: Transforms a positive-definite 3D orthotropic elastic stiffness from material axes to global Voigt coordinates for a constant rotation about axis 3, then returns global stiffness and compliance.
selector: method=rotate; supply angleDegrees and one standard elastic card input (type=engineering with E1/E2/E3, nu12/nu23/nu13, G12/G13/G23; or other supported *ELASTIC type).
limitations: Constitutive tensor transform for a spatially constant rotation about axis 3 only. It does not assign Abaqus element orientations, model spatially varying orientations, assemble elements, solve a boundary-value problem, or claim full Abaqus/CalculiX parity. Host f64 only; explicit GPU requests are unsupported.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Standard linear response spectrum analysis; *RESPONSE SPECTRUM, SUM=SRSS
summary: Opt-in host-f64 response-spectrum estimate: log-log interpolation of a positive acceleration spectrum at each supplied modal frequency, peak modal displacement Gamma*Sa/omega^2, and per-DOF SRSS combination.
selector: analysisType=response-spectrum; provide spectrum=[[frequency_cycles_per_time, spectral_acceleration], ...], modes with frequency or omega, participation, and modeShape; combination defaults to srss.
limitations: Linear peak estimate for an externally supplied mass-normalized modal basis and a single positive acceleration spectrum representing one damping level; only SRSS is implemented. No eigen-extraction, spectrum generation, CQC or other combination rules, time-history response, nonlinear effects, multi-direction summation, or full Abaqus parity. Host-f64 only; explicit CUDA requests fail closed.

abaqusFeature: Rigid body reference point adjustment to center of mass (Abaqus/CAE Adjust point to center of mass at start)
summary: Adds an opt-in adjustment that relocates the rigid-body kinematic pivot to the discrete center of mass computed from supplied nodal masses, so displacement, inertia, constraint blocks, and load moments use that location.
selector: adjustReferenceToCenterOfMass: boolean; requires positive total nodal mass. Existing behavior remains the default.
limitations: Uses only discrete nodal masses and their weighted coordinates; it does not compute continuum element mass, edit an Abaqus model, recover solver reactions, or implement Abaqus analysis steps. A supplied rotational node must remain coincident with the adjusted reference. This helper does not claim full Abaqus or CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Standard Static, Riks automatic arc-length incrementation (*STATIC, RIKS)
summary: Adds opt-in bounded automatic arc-length stepping for the scalar Riks path: failed correctors retry with cutbacks, while accepted increments grow or shrink according to corrector iteration count; accepted sizes are included in the path output.
selector: Set incrementation=automatic and provide arcLength (initial), minArcLength, maxArcLength, and targetIterations. The default remains the existing fixed arcLength behavior.
limitations: Host-f64 scalar cubic/quadratic force law only; this is a standalone continuation demonstrator without finite-element assembly, contact, geometric/material state, or Abaqus parity. The bounded iteration-count controller approximates the feature category and does not reproduce Abaqus internals. Cutbacks are capped at 32; unrecoverable steps fail explicitly.

abaqusFeature: *SHELL SECTION, OFFSET reference-surface offset for S4/S4R shells
summary: Adds an optional homogeneous isotropic shell reference-surface offset to the S4/S4R linear stiffness. Integrates membrane-bending coupling B=z0*A and offset bending D=Dmid+z0^2*A, reports section blocks and energy contribution, and preserves the zero-offset default.
selector: sectionOffset: signed distance z0 from the midsurface in the positive shell-normal direction; admitted range [-thickness/2, thickness/2].
limitations: Single flat four-node linear Reissner-Mindlin facet with homogeneous isotropic material and constant offset only. Layered/composite sections, nonlinear geometry, Abaqus section integration/hourglass formulations, global assembly and full Abaqus/CalculiX parity are not implemented or claimed. Host f64 only; explicit CUDA requests fail closed.

abaqusFeature: *DLOAD distributed pressure (P) on conventional shell elements
summary: Computes the consistent 48-DOF nodal force vector for optional uniform pressure over the reference flat S8/S8R facet; positive pressure acts against the local shell normal.
selector: Optional finite scalar input pressure; omitted pressure leaves pressureLoadLocalDof null.
limitations: One flat, linear S8/S8R facet with uniform pressure integrated on its reference geometry. No follower-load stiffness, nonuniform or hydrostatic pressure, coupled/global assembly, or full Abaqus/CalculiX equivalence is claimed.

abaqusFeature: *EXPANSION, DEFINITION=SECANT, ZERO=reference temperature
summary: Adds uniform 1-D thermoelastic response with a tabulated temperature-dependent isotropic secant expansion coefficient, piecewise-linear interpolation, constant endpoint extrapolation, and fail-closed result validation.
selector: Provide alphaTable as [temperature, coefficient] rows instead of alpha; use tRef and uniform temperature or deltaT. Graded mode with alphaTable is rejected.
limitations: Host-f64 analytic 1-D bar only. Uses the reference temperature as the zero-strain reference and omits Abaqus initial-temperature offset, field-variable dependence, tangent expansion, multidimensional elements, and graded temperature-dependent expansion. This is not full Abaqus or CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: *EXPANSION, TYPE=ISO
summary: For a flat triangular S3/S6 shell with a uniform isotropic thermal expansion coefficient and temperature change, computes the membrane eigenstrain and equivalent full-element nodal load K_membrane times the sampled free-expansion displacement. The thermal load occupies only u/v DOFs and is opt-in.
selector: Provide thermalExpansion and temperatureChange together; both are finite scalars.
limitations: This is a local, flat, small-strain host-f64 element calculation for uniform isotropic expansion with uniform temperature change through thickness. It is not an Abaqus solver, coupled temperature-displacement analysis, temperature-dependent material model, layered-shell thermal calculation, or full equivalence claim. The existing module remains a CalculiX-named implementation; no CalculiX or Abaqus source code was copied.

abaqusFeature: *AMPLITUDE, DEFINITION=SMOOTH STEP
summary: Adds opt-in Abaqus quintic smooth-step interpolation between tabulated amplitude points while preserving the existing linear default, time transforms, and bounded span behavior.
selector: definition: smooth-step (top-level for a single curve or per curve); tabular/linear retains current interpolation
limitations: Evaluates prescribed amplitude curves only; it does not solve an Abaqus model. Smooth-step is host-f64 only and explicit CUDA requests fail closed. The input is span-bounded and rejects queries outside tabulated time; no claim of full Abaqus/CalculiX parity.

abaqusFeature: *AMPLITUDE, DEFINITION=SMOOTH STEP
summary: Adds an opt-in Abaqus-style quintic smooth-step step-time load amplitude to the existing bounded nonlinear static spring solve, with amplitude-aware retries and final equilibrium reporting; linear loading remains the default.
selector: loadAmplitude: "linear" (default) or "smooth-step"
limitations: Host-f64 scalar spring model only; implements the unit 0-to-1 smooth-step curve a=10ξ^3−15ξ^4+6ξ^5 and does not parse Abaqus decks, accept arbitrary amplitude tables, assemble elements, model contact or constraints, or claim Abaqus/CalculiX solver parity.

abaqusFeature: *EQUATION in Abaqus/Standard: first listed nodal variable is eliminated
summary: Adds an opt-in equationConvention mode that prioritizes each linear constraint's first listed dof as the eliminated variable, rejects duplicate or reused eliminated variables, and retains the existing linear constraint solve and residual outputs.
selector: equationConvention='abaqus-standard'
limitations: Small dense linear elastic algebra with explicit matrix inputs only; no Abaqus deck parsing, FE assembly, nonlinear or kinematic constraints, solver procedure, or vendor parity claim. Constraint rows must admit independent requested pivots in this convention.

abaqusFeature: Abaqus/Standard *CONTROLS, CONVERGENCE CHECK=STRICT (paired residual and correction convergence concept)
summary: Adds opt-in residual-and-correction convergence for bounded polynomial nonlinear systems. Convergence requires the residual infinity norm to meet tol and the scaled infinity norm of the last accepted Newton update to meet correctionTol; result history reports correctionNorm. Default residual-only stopping remains intact.
selector: convergence='residual-and-correction' and positive correctionTol; default convergence='residual'
limitations: Host-f64 algebraic polynomial systems only, with dimension at most 16; no FE residual/flux averaging, per-field scaling, element assembly, contact, load incrementation, or full Abaqus convergence semantics. The update scale is ||dx||inf/(1+||x||inf), a local bounded-system normalization.

abaqusFeature: *STEADY STATE DYNAMICS, DIRECT with *DAMPING, STRUCTURAL
summary: Opt-in analytic single-degree-of-freedom harmonic response using structural loss-factor damping, returning displacement amplitude, phase, and dynamic magnification.
selector: method=structural with harmonicOmega, forceAmplitude, mass, and stiffness supplied together
limitations: Closed-form SDOF calculation only; angular frequency is rad/s, force amplitude and phase use a cosine convention, and this does not assemble or solve Abaqus finite-element models or establish solver parity.

abaqusFeature: *STEADY STATE DYNAMICS, DIRECT with material *DAMPING, STRUCTURAL
summary: Solves a supplied discrete complex harmonic response system with a uniform structural loss factor added to viscous or Rayleigh damping; eta contributes i*eta*K to dynamic stiffness.
selector: structuralDamping (nonnegative scalar loss factor)
limitations: Host-f64 algebraic response only for supplied reduced M/C/K matrices; this is not FE assembly, mode extraction, or full Abaqus/CalculiX parity. Structural damping is a single uniform scalar multiplying K; frequency-dependent or element/material-specific factors are not represented. CUDA requests remain unsupported.

abaqusFeature: *SURFACE BEHAVIOR, PRESSURE-OVERCLOSURE=TABULAR
summary: Adds an opt-in monotone piecewise-linear tabular normal pressure-overclosure law for the existing one-pair compliant-body penalty model. Solves d + p(d)/k = approach - gap0 with bounded bisection and returns penetration, pressure, effective stiffness, and equilibrium residual. Existing linear penalty and augmented-Lagrange defaults are preserved.
selector: Set law="tabular" and curve=[[overclosure, pressure], ...]; otherwise law defaults to linear. Tabular law is supported with penalty enforcement only.
limitations: Host-f64 scalar normal contact for one compliant body against a rigid obstacle; no mesh-wide contact search, tangential friction, dynamics, or solver coupling. Curve is required to start at [0,0], have strictly increasing overclosure and nondecreasing pressure, and is limited to 256 points. Final segment slope is continued as in Abaqus tabular behavior. This is a bounded mathematical mapping, not full Abaqus parity.

abaqusFeature: *SURFACE BEHAVIOR, PRESSURE-OVERCLOSURE=TABULAR
summary: Optional bounded piecewise-linear normal pressure-overclosure law for triangular surface contact, with final-segment slope extrapolation and strain energy integrated from the same curve.
selector: pressureOverclosure: array of 2–64 [overclosure, pressure] points beginning [0,0]; omitted input retains the existing epsN linear penalty law.
limitations: Reduced local constitutive calculation for one centroid integration point per flat slave triangle and closest-point projection to flat master triangles. Frictionless, small-sliding and no global constraint enforcement, equilibrium iterations, history, finite-sliding, self-contact, or full Abaqus/CalculiX equivalence. This module retains its CalculiX-style identity and provenance.

abaqusFeature: *TIE rotational degrees of freedom (Tie rotational DOFs if applicable)
summary: Adds opt-in small-rotation-vector tie interpolation on the selected master triangle, reporting rotational constraint residuals and penalty moments while retaining existing translational tie behavior.
selector: tieRotationalDofs=true with slaveRotation and masterRotation arrays; rotationalPenalty optionally sets a separate positive penalty coefficient.
limitations: Reduced host-f64 diagnostic: linear triangular master faces and small rotation vectors only. It does not assemble/enforce global Abaqus constraints, model finite rotations, or reproduce full Abaqus Standard/Explicit tie behavior. The existing module id and CalculiX provenance remain unchanged.

abaqusFeature: *SPRING with SPRING1 ground-referenced linear stiffness
summary: Adds linear ground springs on beam u, v, or theta degrees of freedom at exact mesh nodes; spring forces are reported and stiffness participates in the assembled static solve.
selector: optional top-level springs array of {position, dof, stiffness}; position must coincide with a generated node and stiffness must be positive
limitations: Host-f64 linear static 2D beam formulation only; springs connect one beam nodal DOF to zero-displacement ground, require exact mesh-node positions, and have constant positive real stiffness. No spring-to-spring relative DOFs, nonlinear/temperature-dependent behavior, dynamics, or full Abaqus/CalculiX equivalence.

abaqusFeature: *EXPANSION (constant isotropic thermal expansion)
summary: Extends the existing linear T2D2/T3D2 axial response with uniform constant-coefficient thermal strain, producing free thermal extension, mechanical stress/force under prescribed displacement, and consistent equivalent nodal forces.
selector: For method="axial-response", provide both expansionCoefficient (finite signed secant coefficient) and temperatureChange (finite ΔT); omit both to retain prior behavior.
limitations: Single linear elastic two-node truss element only; uniform temperature change and constant isotropic coefficient. No temperature tables, reference-temperature history, nonlinear/geometric effects, coupled heat transfer, global assembly, or full Abaqus/CalculiX parity is claimed.

abaqusFeature: *TRS, DEFINITION=WLF with *VISCOELASTIC time-domain Prony response
summary: Adds WLF temperature-time shifting to isotropic small-strain Prony stress histories. Per-increment temperatures scale physical time into reduced time; results report both clocks, and temperatures at/below the WLF lower limit produce the instantaneous elastic response.
selector: method=stress with trs={definition:'wlf',referenceTemperature,C1,C2} and temperatures[] aligned with timeIncrements[]
limitations: Clean-room material-point calculation for isotropic, small-strain linear Prony behavior only; temperatures are held constant over each supplied increment. Implements the Abaqus WLF form and lower-temperature cutoff only, not Arrhenius, tabular, USER/UTRS, temperature-dependent instantaneous moduli, coupled thermal analysis, finite-element assembly, or full Abaqus/CalculiX parity.
